title: Annotatio IV §.XIII: Charles the Bald commissions Bertram and Erigena on Lord’s body and blood
pass_a_gloss: As the Age proceeded and rose toward its middle, Charles the Great’s Grandson, at first King of France, soon also a sufficiently illustrious Emperor, CHARLES THE BALD, most eager for Evangelical truth even in the doctrine of the Eucharist, ordered both Bertram the Presbyter and Erigena the Scot to write Treatises on the body and blood of the Lord — from the former of which, since it is still turned in the hands of the learned, we judge it worth the labor to have brought here certain propositions that will illustrate the Eucharistic truth.
pass_b_english: Mid-century: CHARLES THE BALD, eager for Evangelical truth on the Eucharist, ordered Bertram the Presbyter and Erigena the Scot to write treatises on the Lord’s body and blood.
Bertram’s still circulates among the learned — Strimesius draws propositions that illustrate the Eucharistic truth.
source_text: Procedente Seculô & ad medium sui assurgente, Caroli M. Nepos, initiô Rex Franciæ, mox Imperator quoque sat inclitus, CAROLUS CALVUS, veritatis Evangelicæ, etiam in doctrina de Eucharistia percupidus, tum Bertramo Presbytero, tùm Erigena Scoto, de corpore & sanguine Domini Tractatus scribere jussit, ex quorum priori, cum adhuc in manibus eruditorum versetur, quasdam propositiones veritatem Eucharisticam illustraturas, hic adduxisse operæ pretium ducimus.
